svg.title: How your Fandex match works
svg.desc: One label per title, from two questions asked of everything the title is made of: do you seek this kind of thing out, and do you rate it well. The label is where the two land against your usual.
svg.text: How your match works
One label on every title. It answers: how much more likely than usual are you to love this?
It is not a prediction of the number you would give. Nothing here reads the crowd's ratings or what is popular.
1 · WHAT A TITLE IS MADE OF
Fandex breaks every film, show, game or book into its facets:
Platform tags ("PC", "PS5") and noise never count. A tag that sits on almost everything ("action") counts less than a specific one ("steampunk").
2 · TWO QUESTIONS, ASKED OF EVERY FACET
Each facet is checked against your own library twice. Both answers are measured against your usual, never against other people.
Pull · do you seek this out?
Of all the titles Fandex knows with this facet,
the share you have been through,
compared with your usual share of everything.
A title on your wishlist counts half. A facet on only a couple
of titles is pulled toward your usual until there is evidence.
Steampunk · you've seen 46 of 64 · 1.7× your usual share
Tim Burton · 19 of 19 · the most anyone can seek out
Follow a facet and it counts as that maximum. Avoid one, the minimum.
Taste · do you rate it well?
Your average rating for the titles you rated
that carry this facet,
compared with your overall average.
Only ratings you typed yourself. A facet you met once
barely moves; one you met forty times moves fully.
Steampunk · you rate it 7.6 over 41 titles · usual 6.7
Disease · you rate it 8.5 over 11 titles
Games you rate higher than films? That gap is taken out first.
3 · ONLY THE STRONGEST FEW COUNT
A title can carry thirty tags. For each question, only the strongest few of each kind add up:
The rest are still shown in the breakdown, greyed, with the value they would have had. Nothing is hidden.
Some kinds weigh more: a director counts about twice a tag, a setting tag about twice a genre. Those weights are set in one place and printed on every row.
A title you rated is scored as if you had not: its own rating and its own place in the counts are left out, so it can never quote itself.
4 · WHERE THE TWO LAND IS YOUR LABEL
Each question adds up to points above or below your usual. Ten points off either way reads as high or low.
PULL: LOW
PULL: USUAL
PULL: HIGH
TASTE: ABOVE USUAL
TASTE: USUAL
TASTE: BELOW USUAL
Hidden gem
Your usual
Sure thing

You seek it out and
rate it well.
Not your usual pick, but
you rate this kind well.
You seek it out, but you
tend not to love it.
"Your usual" is the biggest cell on purpose: most titles are neither remarkable for you nor against you, and the label says so.
5 · THE ONE NUMBER UNDER THE LABEL
"Films like this: an 8 or more about 1.4× as often as usual."
For titles that got this label, how much more often than usual people rated them 8 or more. Measured on real ratings across
every Fandex user, never guessed. It is odds against your own usual, not a rating.
WHAT NEVER COUNTS
· the crowd's ratings
· how popular a title is
· when it came out
· episodes watched or hours played
· your rating of the title being scored
Only ratings you typed, and what is in your library.
HOW WE CHECK IT
Every change is measured first, per medium:
· does it order your own ratings better
· does it rank what you wishlisted above
what you never touched
· does each label still mean what it says
The goalpost chart on the telemetry page is the running proof.
Fandex match, version 2 · 2026-10-25 · this picture changes whenever the score does
